scope: The footprint of force by state and city: cantonments (DGDE list, states from the PIB state-wise list), DRDO laboratories (cluster pages with addresses), the service command headquarters a PIB release names with its city, CAPF training institutions (CRPF, CISF, ITBP), the police academies (SVPNPA, NEPA) and service academies (NDA, IMA), the seven CFSLs, the ex-OFB companies' factories (MIL, AWEIL, GIL; AVNL partial) and the HQs of BDL, BEML and CSL, one commissionerate (Guwahati), and per-state central-jail facts from NCRB PSI 2023. Three levels of resolution: Union money resolves to the line item; state money resolves to the Police major head per state (and prisons per state from NCRB), with strength and per-capita figures reported: while BPR&D is down; city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (installations, commissionerate entities with reported: strength) and the void. Left out: BSF/SSB/Assam Rifles/NSG sites (blocked or not opened), HAL/BEL/MIDHANI/Yantra/Troop Comforts/India Optel/MDL/GRSE plants (blocked or JS-only), state FSLs (DFSS down), jail locations (NCRB prints none), 14 of ~20 command HQs, cantonment land by state (DGDE AR is an image PDF). No budgets or strength rows are written here; they belong to union-defence, union-home and state-police.

State assignment follows the PIB 2023-03-20 state-wise list (DGDE prints commands, not states); the count of 61 follows the DGDE page. claims.innocentReading: 55 of 61 cantonments predate 1947 and none has been notified since Ajmer in 1962 (DGDE historical perspective); the distribution reflects pre-1962 garrison geography, not any present government's allocation. "Hill station" is not a blanket description (Roorkee, Clement Town and Dehradun are not hill stations), and which six cantonments are post-1947 is not established. Low density in UP and Bihar reflects population size, not fewer installations: UP has the most cantonments of any state (13).
claims.upgradeIf: DGDE already states that six of the 61 were created after Independence and Ajmer (1962) was the last; what is still missing is which six they are, with notification dates from the Gazette

narratives.claim: Cantonments are being abolished so that defence land can be handed to builders.
narratives.strongestCase: Cantonments are being dissolved as a declared policy: PIB 1942023 (24 Jul 2023, RS written reply by RRM Ajay Bhatt) says broad modalities for excision of civil areas in 58 Cantonments were shared with State Governments and that KhasYol was de-notified w.e.f. 27.04.2023; an MoD notification of March 2024 listed areas in 10 cantonments (Dehradun, Clement Town, Deolali, Nasirabad, Babina, Ajmer, Ramgarh, Mathura, Shahjahanpur, Fatehgarh) for excision [reported: Tribune 2024-03-08]; all six HP cantonments were identified in Feb 2025 [reported: Tribune 2025-02-04]. The third modified proposal says that if transferred land is sold or leased, 50 per cent of the income is shared with the Centre [reported: Deccan Chronicle 2024-08-09] — a monetisation clause, which is the one opening for the builders motive.
narratives.strongestCounter: The transferee in every record found is the State Government or municipality, not a private party: civic assets transfer at no cost and ownership of vacant land parcels stays with MoD (Deccan Chronicle 2024-08-09); military areas become exclusive military stations (Tribune 2024-03-08); Khasyol's military area became a military station and its civil area (assets valued ₹6.75 crore, 25 employees) went to the HP government (TOI 2023-04-29; APAC 2023-05-05). MoD's stated reason is uniformity of municipal law between cantonment civil areas and adjoining municipalities, with representations from residents and state governments (PIB 1942023). The excision list spans opposition-run states (Telangana, Kerala, Karnataka, West Bengal, HP), so party does not explain it. Innocent reading: municipal normalisation of colonial-era civil areas, not a sale. Summary: one completed de-notification (Khasyol, 27.04.2023) under a declared 58-cantonment excision programme; no transfer to a private party found. The 2013 CAG audit of defence land (PAC 89th Report) concerned encroachment and records, not sale.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: For it: a gazette or LS answer showing excised or vacant cantonment land allotted, leased or sold to a private developer, or a state's reallocation of transferred land to one. Against it: the first excision completions after the March 2024 notification showing the same state/municipality transferees and MoD retaining vacant land.

symmetryCheck: Footprint is inheritance before it is policy: 61 cantonments were notified under the 1924 Act and earlier, the ordnance factories date from 1801 (Cossipore) onward, and the DRDO labs cluster where their users sit. Running the one lens this file supports — installations per million residents (177 rows nationally) — on BJP-run large states (UP, MH, MP, GJ, RJ, HR, UT, OR, CT, DL, AS, AP, BR, party as commonly reported in 2026) gives 114 installations / 984m = 0.12 per million; on opposition-run states (TN, KL, KA, WB, PB, TG, JK, HP, JH) 57 / 415.6m = 0.14 per million. The two groups are close and both are dominated by colonial-era cantonments and a few research cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata); the gap in either direction is smaller than the coverage gap (BSF, HAL, BEL, prisons absent). Nothing here supports a story of installations following party. Party is text only.
